title: Geospatial & AI Trends: Highlights from 2025 - Geoawesome
headline: 2025 GeoAI Breakthroughs: Predictive Analytics, Automation, and Climate Solutions for Urban and Global Challenges
tldr: The year 2025 saw GeoAI models harness satellite imagery and LLMs to deliver real-time flood detection, crop monitoring, and urban planning insights. These advancements enable cities and policymakers to proactively address climate risks and optimize resource allocation.
significance: These innovations mark a pivotal shift toward data-driven resilience, empowering stakeholders to mitigate environmental threats and enhance sustainable development.

title: Towards the next generation of Geospatial Artificial Intelligence
headline: Charting the Future of Geospatial Artificial Intelligence: Trends, Challenges, and Opportunities
tldr: GeoAI merges geospatial science with AI, rapidly evolving across spatial data science and geography. Understanding recent advances and future directions is essential for leveraging its transformative potential.
significance: This work highlights the critical need to map GeoAI's evolving landscape to guide research and application.

title: Top 5 Geospatial AI Trends to Watch in 2025 - arizton.com
headline: Top 5 GeoAI Trends Shaping 2025: From Foundation Models to Real-Time Flood Detection
tldr: GeoAI is rapidly evolving, with foundation models unlocking new analytical capabilities across satellite imagery and urban planning. Key trends for 2025 include real-time flood detection, precision crop monitoring, and AI-driven change detection in city landscapes.
significance: These trends promise to transform how we monitor and manage Earth's resources, driving smarter decisions in agriculture, urban development, and disaster response.

title: GeoAI and the Next Generation of Geospatial Insights - Geo Week News
headline: GeoAI Revolutionizes Geospatial Analysis: Merging Data, Sensors, and AI for Smarter Insights
tldr: Artificial intelligence is reshaping geospatial science by integrating diverse data sources and advanced analytics. GeoAI empowers organizations to capture, analyze, and act on spatial information faster and more accurately than ever before.
significance: GeoAI unlocks unprecedented precision and speed in mapping, monitoring, and decision-making across sectors.

title: Remote Sensing AI · GitHub
headline: RSandAI GitHub: GeoAI Research Outputs from Istanbul Technical University and Beyond
tldr: The RSandAI GitHub page hosts a collection of remote sensing and AI research outputs supervised by Prof. Dr. Elif SERTEL at Istanbul Technical University. It includes datasets, code, and results that showcase state‑of‑the‑art GeoAI techniques.
significance: It provides an open, reproducible resource for researchers and practitioners to advance GeoAI applications.

title: remote-sensing · GitHub Topics · GitHub
headline: Remote Sensing Change Detection: A Curated Collection of Datasets, Tools, and Competitions
tldr: This repository compiles the latest datasets, tools, methods, review papers, and competitions for remote sensing change detection. It serves as a go-to resource for researchers and practitioners to stay updated and benchmark their models.
significance: It accelerates research by centralizing high-quality resources, enabling faster development and evaluation of change detection algorithms.

title: RuView Free AI WiFi Sensing, ESP32 CSI Radar & Spatial Intelligence
headline: RuView: Open-Source AI WiFi Sensing with ESP32 CSI Radar for Spatial Intelligence
tldr: RuView is an open‑source, edge‑native AI WiFi sensing platform that transforms everyday ESP32 microcontrollers into long‑range spatial radar arrays. By converting ambient high‑frequency radio waves into detailed environmental telemetry, it enables real‑time spatial intelligence without cameras.
significance: RuView democratizes advanced radar sensing, making high‑resolution spatial awareness accessible on low‑cost hardware.

title: remote sensing free download - SourceForge
headline: Explore 38 Open-Source Remote Sensing Projects on SourceForge for Data Scientists
tldr: SourceForge hosts 38 open-source remote sensing projects, offering tools for building production-ready AI agents and models. Users can filter projects and access over 200 Google and third‑party AI models to accelerate development.
significance: These resources empower developers to rapidly prototype and deploy remote sensing solutions without licensing barriers.

title: Raster Vision: An open-source machine learning library for deep ...
headline: Raster Vision: Open-Source GIS and Deep Learning Pipeline for Satellite Image Analysis
tldr: Raster Vision is an open-source framework that unifies GIS and deep learning for remote sensing tasks. It offers configurable pipelines for chip classification, semantic segmentation, and object detection on satellite imagery.
significance: It empowers researchers and developers to build scalable, reproducible computer vision models for Earth observation without reinventing the wheel.

title: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
headline: Learning Task Models from Naturalistic Computer-Use Traces for Auditable AI Agents
tldr: By passively recording screenshots, mouse, and keyboard actions, we can derive symbolic models of everyday work. These models enable AI agents to learn real task flows and allow organizations to audit and reuse work knowledge.
significance: This approach bridges the gap between human workflow understanding and AI automation, ensuring transparency and reusability in workplace AI.

title: DreamHand: Repurposing Video Diffusion Models for Occlusion-Robust Egocentric 3D Hand Motion Recovery
headline: DreamHand: Recovering 3D Hand Motion from Occluded Egocentric Video Using Video Diffusion Models
tldr: DreamHand repurposes video diffusion models to robustly recover metric 3D hand trajectories from egocentric videos, even with severe occlusion and out-of-sight gaps. It achieves this by leveraging efficient inference techniques that avoid heavy, stochastic multi-step sampling.
significance: This approach enables scalable, accurate hand motion capture for embodied AI without requiring extensive labeled data or complex multi-view setups.

title: The Nearby Star Formation and Supernova Histories Reconstructed from Young Star Clusters
headline: Reconstructing Solar Neighborhood Star Formation and Supernova Histories Using Young Star Clusters
tldr: By integrating the past trajectories of Gaia-based young star clusters, we infer the recent star formation rate and core‑collapse supernova frequency in the Solar Neighborhood. The study links cluster ages, masses, and velocities to an axisymmetric Galactic potential to reconstruct a detailed time‑series of local stellar deaths.
significance: This work provides the first high‑resolution reconstruction of local star formation and supernova activity, offering a benchmark for Galactic evolution models.

title: Computational Methods of Wave Propagation for Semiclassical Models of High Harmonic Generation in Bulk Solids
headline: Self‑Consistent Maxwell–Bloch Simulation of High‑Order Harmonic Generation in Bulk Solids
tldr: We develop a self‑consistent computational framework that couples Maxwell’s equations with semiconductor Bloch equations to model nonlinear light‑matter interactions in bulk semiconductors. The method captures high‑order harmonic generation and its propagation, revealing distinct reflected and transmitted harmonic spectra.
significance: This approach provides a predictive tool for designing solid‑state high‑harmonic sources and understanding ultrafast light propagation in materials.

title: A two-point phase recovering with spherical wave reference
headline: Two-Point Phase Recovery Using Spherical Reference Waves in Helmholtz Exterior Problems
tldr: The paper presents two-point formulas to approximate the phase of a radiation solution by measuring the intensity of the combined total solution with a spherical reference wave. These formulas enable phase reconstruction in exterior Helmholtz problems without direct phase measurements.
significance: It offers a practical method for phase retrieval in wave propagation problems, aiding imaging and inverse scattering applications.

title: Zero-Sum Power Factor Games
headline: Zero-Sum Power Factor Games: Controlling Voltage with Reactive Power Pre-Selection
tldr: Operators can limit voltage deviations by remotely setting DER reactive power before active injections occur. This zero-sum game ensures constant power factor compliance per IEEE 1547-2018 while mitigating unpredictable active power fluctuations.
significance: It provides a proactive strategy to maintain grid stability amid volatile renewable generation.

title: A blind spot in transverse BAO calibration
headline: Blind Spot in Transverse BAO Calibration: Hidden Degeneracy with r_d h
tldr: Transverse BAO measurements rely on a calibration that cannot be constrained by cosmological data alone. A constant error in the BAO scale is degenerate with r_d h, making it invisible to standard analyses.
significance: This hidden degeneracy can bias cosmological parameter estimates, undermining the precision of BAO-based constraints.

title: Physical-Support Confidence Sets for Highly Coherent Dictionaries
headline: Resolving Physical Support Conflicts in Highly Coherent Dictionaries for Sparse Pursuit
tldr: We introduce a resolution-aware method that constructs confidence sets for the physical support of dictionary atoms, even when the dictionary is highly coherent. This approach reconciles calibration inconsistencies and yields more reliable interpretations in sparse pursuit applications.
significance: By providing statistically grounded support confidence sets, the method improves the interpretability and robustness of dictionary-based signal recovery in noisy, highly coherent settings.

title: QED radiative effects in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering: traditional and factorized approaches
headline: Comparing Traditional and Factorized QED Radiative Corrections for SIDIS Nucleon Structure
tldr: This study compares traditional and factorized approaches to QED radiative corrections in semi‑inclusive deep‑inelastic scattering. The authors find that the factorized method provides a more accurate extraction of parton distributions, especially at low transverse momentum.
significance: Accurate treatment of QED radiation is essential for precise determination of parton distribution functions from SIDIS experiments.

title: Non-Minimally Coupled Warm Inflation in the Defining Frame
headline: Warm Inflation Dynamics in F(Φ)R Theories: Defining vs Einstein Frame Analysis
tldr: We study warm inflation in scalar‑tensor F(Φ)R gravity in the defining frame and translate the dynamics to the Einstein frame. The dissipation ratio is reduced by modified‑gravity effects, showing that the effective warm‑inflation behavior can be consistently described in either frame.
significance: This work clarifies how modified gravity influences dissipation during warm inflation, aiding the interpretation of early‑universe models.

title: Programmable cavity QED with a fiber-integrated atomic array
headline: Fiber-Integrated Tweezer Array Enables Programmable Cavity QED with Rubidium Atoms
tldr: Researchers integrated a twelve‑site ^87Rb optical tweezer array into a high‑cooperativity fiber cavity, achieving strong, site‑resolved atom‑photon coupling. This platform opens pathways for scalable quantum networks and programmable quantum optics experiments.
significance: It demonstrates a scalable, controllable interface between neutral atoms and cavity QED, bridging tweezer arrays and high‑cooperativity cavities.

title: Group-theoretic treatment of strong light-matter coupling with an arbitrary number of excitations
headline: Group-Theoretic Approach to Multi-Excitation Strong Light-Matter Coupling
tldr: The paper extends polariton theory beyond single-excitation limits by employing group-theoretic methods, enabling accurate modeling of many-excitation dynamics. This framework paves the way for exploring complex light-matter phenomena in microcavities.
significance: It provides a powerful mathematical tool to capture multi-excitation physics, crucial for designing next-generation photonic devices.

title: G-CARL: Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning for Patient-Oriented Medical Report Interpretation
headline: G-CARL: Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning for Personalized Medical Report Interpretation
tldr: We present G-CARL, a framework that aligns reward learning with evidence-based checklists to generate patient-friendly interpretations of medical reports. The approach combines foundation model capabilities with grounded factuality and context-aware communication, addressing gaps in current vision-language tasks.
significance: G-CARL advances patient-centered care by ensuring medical reports are both factually accurate and easily understood by patients.

title: Large Sample Properties of Higher Order Markov Models
headline: Central Limit Theorem for Growing-Order Markov Chains on Finite Alphabets
tldr: We prove a central limit theorem for additive functionals of Markov chains whose order grows with sample size. The result uses return-time decompositions and requires mild ergodicity and sparsity conditions.
significance: The work extends classical Markov chain asymptotics to high-order models, enabling rigorous inference for complex time-series data.

title: An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
headline: Agentic Workflow Combines Chatbot Data Collection and Predictive Modeling for Travel
tldr: This study introduces a three-agent system that merges conversational data gathering, structured data processing, and behavior prediction for travel mode choices. A chatbot-administered, image-augmented survey demonstrates its effectiveness in real-world data collection.
significance: By integrating data collection and modeling, the approach reduces evaluation gaps and enhances predictive accuracy in travel behavior research.

title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
headline: AI4AI-Bench: Evaluating LLM Agents for Recursive Self-Improvement in Algorithmic Design
tldr: Recursive self‑improvement asks whether an AI can enhance the training algorithm that creates future AIs, thereby improving the compute‑capability exchange rate. AI4AI‑Bench tests LLM agents on this process, measuring how better objectives or update rules propagate across successive runs.
significance: Benchmarking RSI in LLM agents provides a systematic way to assess whether training improvements can be self‑propagated, informing safe and efficient AI evolution.

title: Projecting BrowseComp-Plus onto ClimbMix: Toward More Realistic Corpora for Agentic Search
headline: Expanding BrowseComp-Plus with ClimbMix for Realistic Agentic Search Corpora
tldr: The BrowseComp-Plus benchmark replaced web search with a 100K‑document corpus, but its evidence and distractors were both drawn from the benchmark’s own queries. By projecting this corpus onto ClimbMix, researchers aim to create more realistic, diverse datasets for evaluating agentic search systems.
significance: This work enhances benchmark realism, enabling more robust evaluation of language models in open‑domain search tasks.

title: Pandora's AI Model Routing Box: Efficient Allocation with Costly Value Estimation
headline: Efficient AI Routing: Balancing Specialist Selection and Estimation Costs for Low-Cost Queries
tldr: Routing queries to specialist AI models can improve performance, but estimating each model’s value incurs cost. This paper proposes a cost‑aware routing framework that balances estimation expense against expected gains, enabling efficient, low‑cost query handling.
significance: It demonstrates a practical method for deploying heterogeneous AI systems that optimally allocate queries while accounting for the cost of value estimation.

title: Explainable Transformer Models for Clinical Prediction Tasks on Structured Electronic Health Records
headline: Explainable BERT for Predicting Clinical Outcomes from Structured EHR Timelines
tldr: BERT-LER is a transformer model pretrained on 75M patient EHR timelines that incorporates quantitative lab data and provides event‑level interpretability for clinical prediction tasks. The model achieves state‑of‑the‑art performance on multiple outcome prediction benchmarks while allowing clinicians to trace predictions back to specific medical events.
significance: It demonstrates that large‑scale transformer models can be both accurate and interpretable for real‑world EHR data.

title: MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
headline: MidTool: Enhancing LLMs with Mid-Training Data Synthesis for Tool Use
tldr: MidTool presents a novel mid-training data synthesis approach that enhances LLMs' tool-use capabilities. The method improves reasoning-intensive tasks and agentic performance in software engineering contexts.
significance: This work demonstrates that targeted mid-training can substantially elevate LLMs' practical tool-use abilities, paving the way for more autonomous AI systems.

title: Inter-X++: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Human-Human Interaction Analysis
headline: Inter-X++: A Comprehensive Multimodal Benchmark Dataset for Human-Human Interaction Analysis
tldr: Inter-X++ introduces a richly annotated, high-fidelity multimodal dataset capturing human-human interactions, addressing gaps in kinematics and hand gesture representation. The benchmark enables robust evaluation of models for interaction understanding and paves the way for advanced digital human systems.
significance: By providing high-quality multimodal annotations and a standardized evaluation protocol, Inter-X++ accelerates research toward more natural and context-aware digital humans.

title: Imaging the vacuum fluctuations of a quantum field
headline: Visualizing Quantum Vacuum Fluctuations in Field Snapshots Using Advanced Imaging Techniques
tldr: Quantum fields exhibit random spatial patterns even in vacuum due to Heisenberg uncertainty. New imaging methods capture these fluctuations, revealing fundamental physics and potential applications.
significance: Imaging vacuum fluctuations provides direct insight into quantum vacuum energy and informs technologies ranging from precision measurement to quantum computing.

title: The Additive Arithmetic of Linear Orders
headline: Arithmetic of Linear Orders: Euclidean Algorithm and Lindenbaum Division in Theory
tldr: We develop a systematic arithmetic for the class of linear orders under ordered sum, introducing a Euclidean algorithm for pairs that almost commute. The work unifies classical theorems, including Lindenbaum's division, and yields new results on additive structure.
significance: This framework provides a unified algebraic foundation for linear order theory, extending classical results and enabling new insights into additive combinatorics.

title: An Optical Illusion: High Electron Densities Create Extremely Metal-Poor Galaxy Impostors
headline: High Electron Densities Mimic Extremely Metal-Poor Galaxies: An Optical Illusion
tldr: JWST observations revealed galaxies that appear extremely metal-poor, but high electron densities can mimic low metallicity signatures. This study shows that careful analysis of ionized gas conditions is essential to avoid misclassifying galaxies as first-generation systems.
significance: The work cautions against overinterpreting low-metallicity signatures in early galaxies, refining the search for truly primordial galaxies.

title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
headline: ConceptGuard: A New Benchmark for Context‑Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
tldr: ConceptGuard introduces a realistic evaluation framework that tests LLMs’ ability to forget context‑dependent knowledge without compromising unrelated facts. It moves beyond simple fact recall, addressing the nuanced demands of real‑world unlearning.
significance: By revealing gaps in current unlearning methods, ConceptGuard pushes the development of safer, more controllable language models.

title: 4DAnyone: Create Anyone in 4D from a Casual Monocular Video
headline: 4DAnyone: Reconstructing 4D Humans from Uncalibrated Monocular Video
tldr: 4DAnyone generates reconstruction‑grade, multiview‑consistent videos from a casual monocular clip and lifts them into 4D Gaussian Splatting, enabling 4D human reconstruction without camera calibration. It overcomes the view‑consistency limitations of existing diffusion models when scaling to dozens of target views.
significance: This framework democratizes high‑fidelity 4D human reconstruction, allowing realistic avatars to be created from everyday videos without specialized hardware.

title: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
headline: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
tldr: WithEveryone introduces a unified framework that simultaneously plans spatial layout and grounds identities for group image generation, ensuring each specified person appears in the correct location with accurate facial features. The method aligns noisy predicted faces through training-time identity losses, improving reliability over existing models.
significance: This approach addresses a key limitation in multi-person image synthesis, enabling more accurate and scalable generation of complex scenes with multiple identities.

title: Swift-Image: Exploring the Performance Frontier of Compact Unified Image Generation Models
headline: Swift-Image: Compact Unified Diffusion Model for Text-to-Image and Editing
tldr: Swift-Image is a 6B single-stream DiT that unifies text-to-image generation and image editing in a single compact model. Through a progressive training pipeline and systematic engineering, it pushes the performance frontier while staying within a constrained computational budget.
significance: It demonstrates that small, efficient diffusion models can achieve competitive performance across multiple vision tasks, enabling broader deployment.

title: Production of quarkonium pairs via the fragmentation mechanism
headline: Fragmentation Mechanisms Drive Quarkonium Pair Production in High-Energy Collisions and Beyond
tldr: We analyze how fragmentation processes contribute to the production of quarkonium pairs in hadronic collisions. A microscopic perturbative model for dihadron fragmentation functions is developed to quantify the double-hadron mechanism.
significance: This work provides a quantitative framework for understanding quarkonium pair production, essential for interpreting LHC data and testing QCD factorization.

title: The Memory Hidden in Response Fluctuations: Trajectory-Level Fluctuation-Response Theory and Inequalities for Non-Markovian Jump Dynamics
headline: Memory Effects in Non-Markovian Jump Dynamics: A Trajectory-Level Fluctuation-Response Theory
tldr: We formulate a fluctuation-response framework for non-Markovian jump processes directly on the event record, deriving exact stochastic equations for transition counts. This approach reveals how memory destroys closed master equations yet still permits precise response inequalities.
significance: The work provides a rigorous tool to analyze memory-driven nonequilibrium systems, bridging trajectory statistics and response theory.

title: Competing triangular and stripe supersolid orders in a dipolar quantum gas
headline: Competing Triangular and Stripe Supersolid Orders Observed in a Dipolar Quantum Gas
tldr: Researchers have experimentally realized two distinct supersolid patterns—triangular and stripe—in a dipolar quantum gas. This observation confirms theoretical predictions and opens avenues for exploring exotic quantum phases.
significance: The discovery provides the first experimental evidence of competing spatial orders in dipolar supersolids, validating complex phase diagrams predicted by theory.

title: $TCP_α$: Margin-Controlled Confidence estimation for reliable Music Information Retrieval
headline: Margin‑Controlled Confidence Estimation for Reliable Music Retrieval
tldr: Deep neural networks often overestimate confidence, misleading users. The proposed TCP_α method trains a lightweight auxiliary head to generate more reliable confidence scores for music information retrieval tasks.
significance: TCP_α offers a practical, post‑hoc solution to improve trustworthiness of MIR predictions by controlling confidence margins.

title: Strange Metal Hall Effect in Underdoped BaFe$_2$(As$_{1-x}$P$_x$)$_2$
headline: Hall Effect Reveals Doping-Independent Behavior in Strange Metal BaFe2(As1−xPx)2
tldr: The study measures the Hall effect in underdoped BaFe2(As1−xPx)2 and finds a doping‑independent contribution that persists across a wide temperature range. This suggests a universal transport mechanism in strange metals beyond the quasiparticle picture.
significance: It provides new insight into the fundamental physics of high‑temperature superconductors by identifying a universal Hall response in the strange metal regime.

title: Spin-torque microwave detectors of positive rectangular pulse signals
headline: Spin-Torque Microwave Detectors Operate in Linear and Nonlinear Pulse Regimes
tldr: We study spin-torque microwave detectors driven by positive rectangular current pulses and identify linear and nonlinear operation regimes. The time-averaged voltage scales linearly with pulse amplitude in the linear regime and shows distinct behavior in the nonlinear regime.
significance: This work provides a framework for optimizing spin-torque detectors for high-speed microwave sensing applications.

title: A comparison between ceiling-mounted FMCW, IR-UWB and Wi-Fi radar for in-bedroom human activity monitoring and sleep interruption detection
headline: Comparing Ceiling-Mounted FMCW, IR-UWB, and Wi-Fi Radar for Bedside Activity Monitoring
tldr: This study evaluates three RF sensing technologies—FMCW radar, IR-UWB, and Wi-Fi—in identical bedroom setups to detect human activity and sleep interruptions. Results highlight trade-offs in accuracy, latency, and deployment complexity, guiding future contact‑free health monitoring systems.
significance: It provides the first side‑by‑side benchmark of these radar modalities under controlled conditions, informing design choices for non‑intrusive sleep and activity monitoring.

title: Probabilistic Representation and Convergence of Gromov-Wasserstein Gradient Flows
headline: Probabilistic Gromov–Wasserstein Gradient Flow Convergence
tldr: The paper derives a probabilistic representation for the inner product Gromov–Wasserstein gradient flow of relative entropy with respect to a Gaussian measure, proving convergence and connecting it to diffusion processes and PDEs.
significance: It links optimal transport theory with stochastic PDEs, providing new analytical tools for metric measure spaces.

title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
headline: SPADE: Self-Play RL for Adaptive Synthetic Environments with LLMs
tldr: SPADE introduces a self-play reinforcement learning framework that lets a single large language model generate and solve increasingly diverse synthetic goals. By continuously expanding its goal pool, the agent adapts to scaling challenges and improves performance without external supervision.
significance: This approach enables language agents to autonomously evolve their training curriculum, overcoming the limitations of static goal distributions.

title: Qualified Cross-References as a Verification Method: The Normative Environment of the EU AI Act
headline: Using Qualified Cross-References to Verify EU AI Act Compliance Framework
tldr: The paper proposes a method for representing legal cross-references with qualified links that capture legal character, supporting provisions, and conditions. This approach ensures consistency and verifiability across the EU AI Act’s normative environment.
significance: It offers a systematic way to encode and verify legal relationships, enhancing transparency and compliance in AI governance.

title: The Structured Totient Preimage Problem: Reconstruction, Collisions, and Cryptographic Implications
headline: Reconstructing Primes from Totient Products: The Structured Totient Preimage Problem
tldr: The Structured Totient Preimage (STP) problem asks to recover k distinct λ‑bit primes given only the product of their decremented values, x = ∏(p_i−1). While verifiable efficiently, the problem’s reconstruction hardness has implications for cryptographic constructions.
significance: STP provides a new hard problem that could underpin cryptographic primitives and offers insight into prime reconstruction challenges.

title: SiNMULI: Novel Signed Network Approach for Malicious URL Identification
headline: SiNMULI: Signed Network Model Enhances Detection of Malicious URLs in Real-Time
tldr: SiNMULI introduces a novel signed network framework that captures relationships between URLs and user interactions, improving phishing detection accuracy. The model leverages graph-based features and achieves state‑of‑the‑art performance on benchmark datasets.
significance: By modeling malicious URL propagation as a signed network, SiNMULI offers a scalable, interpretable solution that outperforms traditional machine‑learning classifiers.

title: PartialBiGrasp: Inferring Hidden Local Geometry for Bimanual Grasping from Partial Views
headline: PartialBiGrasp: Inferring Hidden Geometry for Dual-Arm Grasping from Partial Views
tldr: PartialBiGrasp introduces a method to infer hidden local geometry for bimanual grasping using only partial point cloud views. By predicting sparse graspable regions from incomplete data, it enables dual-arm robots to manipulate large, complex objects that were previously ungraspable with single-arm approaches.
significance: This approach expands the capability of dual-arm robots to handle large, geometrically complex objects by overcoming the limitation of incomplete sensor data.

title: Diffuse HI emission in the circumgalactic medium of NGC891 and NGC4565 - III: azimuthal profiles
headline: Azimuthal Profiles of Diffuse HI Emission in the CGM of NGC891 and NGC4565
tldr: The study maps the inner neutral circumgalactic medium around NGC891 and NGC4565, revealing a 360° view of HI inflows and co-rotation within 25–30 kpc. It confirms that minor‑axis inflows and major‑axis co‑rotation persist across the full azimuthal range.
significance: These observations provide the most complete azimuthal characterization of neutral gas in nearby galaxy halos, refining models of gas accretion and disk–halo interaction.

title: A Fast Deterministic Algorithm for $(Δ+1)$-edge coloring in CONGEST
headline: Deterministic (Δ+1)-Edge Coloring Achieved in Polylogarithmic Rounds on CONGEST in Distributed Setting
tldr: A recent deterministic algorithm finds a (Δ+1)-edge coloring in poly(Δ, log n) rounds in the CONGEST model, improving upon previous randomized methods. The technique leverages new combinatorial insights to overcome communication bottlenecks.
significance: This result demonstrates that optimal edge coloring can be achieved deterministically in near-linear time on distributed networks, closing a long-standing gap between theory and practice.

title: The regular pentagon is canonically Ramsey
headline: Canonical Ramsey Property of the Regular Pentagon Revealed
tldr: Researchers proved that any colouring of a sufficiently large point set contains either a monochromatic or rainbow copy of a regular pentagon. This extends the canonical Ramsey theory beyond triangles to more complex polygons.
significance: The result deepens our understanding of geometric configurations in combinatorial geometry, showing that even regular pentagons exhibit canonical Ramsey behaviour.

title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control
headline: Hydra-0: Generalist World Model Using Action Flow for Cross-Embodiment Control
tldr: We present Hydra-0, a generalist world model that encodes robot actions as pixel motion, enabling shared visual interfaces across embodiments and tasks. The model achieves significant reductions in robot- and object-motion error compared to prior methods.
significance: Hydra-0 demonstrates that action flow can unify world modeling and control across diverse robots and environments, paving the way for more adaptable autonomous systems.

title: From Corpora to Co-Evolving Capabilities: Capability-Centric Data Design for Generalist Image Generation
headline: Designing Data for Generalist Image Generation: A Capability-Centric Pipeline Approach
tldr: The paper introduces a new data design paradigm that aligns heterogeneous supervision with interdependent generative capabilities, enabling more efficient training of generalist image generation models. By curating corpora in a capability-centric manner, the authors demonstrate improved performance across multiple generation tasks compared to conventional task-specific datasets.
significance: This work provides a scalable framework for building versatile image generation systems that can adapt to diverse tasks without retraining separate models.

title: Analytic Continuation of Conformal Integrals in Momentum Space
headline: Analytic Continuation of Conformal Triple‑K Integrals for Higher‑Point Correlators in Momentum Space
tldr: This work extends the analytic continuation of triple‑K integrals, key building blocks of conformal correlators, to arbitrary complex dimensions. The results provide a systematic framework for evaluating higher‑point functions in momentum space.
significance: It offers a unified method to compute conformal correlators, enhancing our ability to test holographic dualities and conformal bootstrap techniques.

title: Multi-Agent AI System for Radiology Report Structuring and Quality Assurance with Independent Radiologist Evaluation
headline: Multi-Agent AI System Enhances Radiology Report Structuring and Quality Assurance
tldr: We developed a locally deployed multi-agent AI pipeline that structures and verifies radiology reports from CT scans. Evaluation on 638 reports from 15 radiologists shows improved consistency and reduced errors.
significance: This study demonstrates that a multi-agent AI framework can reliably standardize radiology documentation, potentially improving clinical workflow and patient safety.

title: Ultrafast and high resolution spatial light modulation for cold atoms
headline: Ultrafast, High-Resolution Spatial Light Modulation Enables Precise Control of Cold Atom Arrays
tldr: A new ultrafast spatial light modulator provides high-resolution optical shaping, allowing precise local control of programmable ultracold atom arrays. This advancement accelerates quantum computation and simulation by enabling rapid, accurate manipulation of atomic qubits.
significance: The technology dramatically improves the scalability and fidelity of quantum processors based on cold atoms.

title: Revisiting the Intra-Team Communication Method to Elicit Level-k Reasoning in Beauty Contests and 11-20 Games
headline: Revisiting Intra-Team Communication for Level‑k Reasoning in Beauty Contests and 11‑20 Games
tldr: We use intra‑team communication to uncover level‑0 strategies in beauty contests and 11‑20 games. The results show how higher‑level players evaluate these baseline actions.
significance: It advances understanding of bounded rationality by linking communication methods to level‑k modeling.

title: Planning Against Learning in Rank-1 Games
headline: Strategic Planning Against Learners in Rank‑1 Games: Optimizing for Replicator Dynamics
tldr: In repeated multi‑agent settings, a player can anticipate and shape a learner’s future actions by planning against the learner’s adaptation dynamics. The paper shows that optimizing against the continuous‑time Replicator Dynamics is computationally tractable for rank‑1 games.
significance: This work bridges game theory and online learning, enabling opponents to strategically influence learning agents in a tractable manner.
